cardinality.rule: Events.STACK_VIEWPORT_SCROLL: no event fires for each scroll: listen to NEW_IMAGE for the slice that is shown and to CAMERA_MODIFIED for the camera; a scroll stopped at the first or the last slice fires SCROLL_OUT_OF_BOUNDS

Events.VOLUME_VIEWPORT_SCROLL: no event fires for each scroll: listen to NEW_IMAGE for the slice that is shown and to CAMERA_MODIFIED for the camera; a scroll stopped at the first or the last slice fires SCROLL_OUT_OF_BOUNDS

Events.STACK_SCROLL_OUT_OF_BOUNDS: SCROLL_OUT_OF_BOUNDS fires for a stack, a volume in any orientation and a video, from utilities.scroll and from viewport.scroll, on the element and on eventTarget, and not with loop; the detail is { viewportId, renderingEngineId, displaySetId, volumeId, sliceIndex, numberOfSlices, delta, direction, imageId }, and sliceIndex is the position the scroll stopped at: detail.direction is detail.delta, and detail.imageIdIndex (the position before the scroll) has no key

Events.VOLUME_VIEWPORT_SCROLL_OUT_OF_BOUNDS: SCROLL_OUT_OF_BOUNDS fires for a stack, a volume in any orientation and a video, from utilities.scroll and from viewport.scroll, on the element and on eventTarget, and not with loop; the detail is { viewportId, renderingEngineId, displaySetId, volumeId, sliceIndex, numberOfSlices, delta, direction, imageId }, and sliceIndex is the position the scroll stopped at: detail.currentImageId is detail.imageId, numScrollSteps is numberOfSlices - 1, and currentStepIndex, desiredStepIndex and viewport have no key (getEnabledElementByIds(viewportId, renderingEngineId).viewport)
